newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Jospin, Juppe meet for handover.
newsitem.headline: France's Jospin, Juppe meet for handover.

text.p: Socialist French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin formally took office on Tuesday, meeting his conservative Gaullist predecessor, Alain Juppe, for a handover.
The two men exchanged a cordial handshake and posed smiling for photographers in the courtyard of the prime minister's Matignon office on Paris' Left Bank.

Socialist party spokesman Francois Hollande said Jospin would form a smaller, more feminine cabiet which he hoped would include representatives of all the left-wing parties which won Sunday's parliamentary election, including the Communists.
Jospin had an hour-long meeting with Communist leader Robert Hue on Tuesday morning to discuss the formation of the government.

The Communists said on Monday they wanted to participate but sought undertakings from the Socialists to raise the national minimum wage by eight percent, take first steps to cut the work week to 35 hours from 39 and ensure there would be no further austerity to qualify for a single European currency.
But an aide to Jospin said he had told Hue he wanted "a yes or no answer without conditions".
